{{Quote|Look at this. All the database says is: 'Abafar, information on Planet:Void.'|Meebur Gascon|<ref name="Sunny" />}}
'''Abafar''' was a remote [[Desert/Legends|desert]] world within the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. The [[Planet/Legends|planet]] was scarcely populated and mostly covered in a featureless expanse known as [[The Void/Legends|The Void]].

==Description==
===Geography===
{{Quote|Wait a minute, there is no sun! How do we know which direction we're going?|Meebur Gascon|<ref name="Sunny" />}}
[[File:AbafarSettlement-ASDitV.png|thumb|left|250px|Detail of the geography of Abafar.]]
Abafar was a hot and remote [[Desert/Legends|desert]] world<ref name="SWE" /> located within the [[Abafar system/Legends|Abafar system]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]' [[Sprizen sector/Legends|Sprizen sector]].<ref name="EAOC" /> Its geography mostly consisted of empty, featureless plains, known as [[The Void/Legends|The Void]], and a few [[City/Legends|urban]] settlements, such as the [[Mining/Legends|mining]] town of [[Pons Ora/Legends|Pons Ora]].<ref name="SWE" /> Large geographic indentations crisscrossed its surface, although they were not clearly visible from [[Realspace/Legends|space]] with the naked [[Eye/Legends|eye]]. The [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] database file on Abafar revealed these markings.<ref name="Sunny" /> Even though a desert, the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] possessed [[Water/Legends|water]]<ref name="SW.com trivia" /> and was one of the few suppliers of a type of volatile fuel known as [[Rhydonium/Legends|Rhydonium]].<ref name="SWE" />

According to Republic data on the planet, Abafar had a polar diameter of 12 11 714, equatorial distance of 1625856 and a surface area of 580 025 700, being 14 11 000 of these made up of land area and 80 40 000 of sea area. Republic files had no information on population count, and indicated that the lowest point was located 850 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] below sea level and the deepest point in the planet was at 44585. 25648".<ref name="SW.com trivia" /><ref name="no unit" />

The town of Pons Ora, built lower than the surrounding ground level, was notable for its extraction of Rhydonium. Although the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] itself was scarcely populated, the settlement featured a wide array of immigrated [[Species/Legends|species]], such as [[Aleena/Legends|Aleena]], [[Aqualish/Legends|Aqualish]], [[Dug/Legends|Dug]], [[Human/Legends|Human]], [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] and a [[Unidentified tentacle-faced species/Legends|tentacle-faced]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. Commercial activity was practiced, as evidenced by the existence of [[Game Go/Legends|Game Go]] and the diner [[Power Sliders/Legends|Power Sliders]].<ref name="MIA" />

Due to particulates in the [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]], sunlight reflected on the chalky, white surface produced a diffuse orange sky, and these conditions, combined with regolith properties in made the white dust on the ground hazy. Because of this, it was nearly impossible to cast shadows, leave tracks and tell the direction or time of day.<ref name="SWE" />

===Fauna===
{{Quote|We've got to stop following my training or your programming and follow the birds' instincts! Grab hold!|Meebur Gascon to WAC-47|<ref name="Sunny" />}}
Abafar, due to its harsh conditions, had limited bio-diversity. The seemingly static landscape would at times be disrupted by the sudden stampede of a certain species of limber, flightless [[Bird/Legends|birds]],<ref name="Sunny" /> known as [[Void Strider]]s.<ref name="EG" /> The striders occasionally traveled in large packs across its barren expanses. The birds did not seem to mind the presence of other [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] species and [[Droid/Legends|droids]].<ref name="Sunny" /> Additionally, in urban settlements such as Pons Ora, a particular species of bug thrived on organic matter such as leftover food and garbage.<ref name="MIA" />

==History==
{{Quote|Well, this is a fine mess you mechs got us into.|Meebur Gascon|<ref name="Sunny" />}}
[[File:Battle_droids-MIA.png|thumb|left|250px|Separatist battle droids patrol the dusty streets of Pons Ora.]]
During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] installed a [[Rhydonium mining installation/Legends|Rhydonium mining installation]] on the planet, specifically in Pons Ora.<ref name="SWE" />

At around [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],<ref name="DS1">[[Darth Maul — Death Sentence 1|''Darth Maul — Death Sentence'' 1]]</ref> the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] [[D-Squad/Legends|D-Squad]], led by [[Meebur Gascon/Legends|Meebur Gascon]], crash-landed on Abafar following a [[Maxillipede shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] engine malfunction in the comet-filled region. The members of D-Squad wandered for some time and came across the ruins of an unidentified trading vessel. Shortly afterwards, Colonel Meebur Gascon had an outbreak of lunacy, so [[WAC-47/Legends|WAC-47]] remained behind with him while the other [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droids]] moved on.<ref name="Sunny" />

The members of D-Squad regrouped after splitting up in Pons Ora. Soon after, they found a [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commando]] named [[Gregor/Legends|Gregor]] who helped the droids of D-Squad infiltrate the Separatist installation, steal a [[Nu-class attack shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] and escape the planet.<ref name="MIA" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Abafar_full.png|thumb|Holographic depiction of Abafar]]
{{Quote|We do one episode called 'The Void,' which is basically a whole exploration of Mœbius and his artwork style, which is a big influence on ''Star Wars''. So it's really abstract, and we were out on the edge. It was like the white room in THX. It was really experimental stuff.|Dave Filoni, excerpt from [[The ForceCast]] at 1:36:08|<ref name="September 14 ForceCast">{{WebCite|url=http://www.forcecast.net/story/home/Weekly_ForceCast_September_14_2012_148041.asp|text=ForceCast.net: Weekly ForceCast: September 14, 2012|author=Jimmy|date=2012-09-14|archivedate=20160410184406}}</ref>}}
The planet Abafar was first mentioned in the "[[Launchpad|''Launch Pad'']]" section of the magazine [[Star Wars Insider 138|''Star Wars Insider'' 138]], published [[December]] [[2012]].<ref name="launchpad">{{InsiderCite|138|Launchpad|Launch Pad}}</ref> Its first appearance, however, came with "[[A Sunny Day in the Void]]," an episode in the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series, which aired December 7, 2012 in Canada and the following day in the United States.<ref name="Explore: A Sunny Day in the Void">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/a-sunny-day-in-the-void-episode-guide|text="A Sunny Day in the Void" Episode Guide &#124; The Clone Wars}}</ref> Abafar's visuals were based on the work of the French comic artist [[Wikipedia:Jean Giraud|Jean Giraud]], better known as Mœbius.<ref name="September 14 ForceCast" />
